faqs.question: How tall does a basement ceiling need to be for living space?
faqs.answer: Under Oregon's 2023 residential code, new living space needs a ceiling of at least 7 feet. Converting an existing basement needs at least 6 feet 8 inches, and beams or ducts may come down to 6 feet 4 inches. Your contractor confirms what applies with the permit.

faqs.question: Can I put a bedroom in my basement?
faqs.answer: Often, if it meets code. Oregon's 2023 residential code requires an emergency escape opening in each basement bedroom, with at least 5.7 square feet of clear opening and a sill no higher than 44 inches. Your contractor builds that; we design the room around it.

faqs.question: How much does basement design cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the scope, from a single consultation to full-service design. We quote after the discovery call. Our guide to [what an interior designer costs in Portland](/blog/interior-designer-cost-portland) explains how designers usually charge.

faqs.question: How do you make a basement feel less dark?
faqs.answer: Layer the light: ceiling lights for the whole room, lamps at seating, and wall lights where people walk. Lighter colors, mirrors near windows and rugs that warm up hard floors help too.

faqs.question: Do you handle the construction?
faqs.answer: No. We design the space and choose the finishes, lighting and furniture. A licensed contractor does the construction and handles permits.

factChecks.claim: Converted space rule applies to an existing basement
factChecks.quote: Conversion of existing nonhabitable space, such as a basement or attic
Beams, girders, ducts or other obstructions in basements containing habitable space shall be permitted to project to within 6 feet 4 inches (1931 mm) of the finished floor.

factChecks.claim: Escape opening required in each basement sleeping room (R310.1 as amended Oct. 1, 2024; this sentence was kept)
factChecks.quote: Where basements contain one or more sleeping rooms, an emergency escape and rescue opening shall be required in each sleeping room.
Emergency escape and rescue openings shall have a net clear opening of not less than 5.7 square feet
The minimum net clear opening height dimension shall be 24 inches (610 mm). The minimum net clear opening width dimension shall be 20 inches (508 mm).
Emergency escape and rescue openings shall have the bottom of the clear opening not greater than 44 inches (1118 mm) above the finished floor.
The horizontal area of the area well shall be not less than 9 square feet (0.9 m 2 ), with a horizontal projection and width of not less than 36 inches (914 mm).
The headroom in stairways shall be not less than 6 feet 8 inches (2032 mm)
